doc.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995

title: Integration in music and bandleaders
summary: Asked about integration, Tate cites Jimmy Dorsey's June Richmond, Tommy Dorsey's Charlie Shavers and Sy Oliver, and integrated small groups.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: I want to ask you a question about jazz. You know we had talked, and you had talked about this too, how that in the early years of jazz of course before a certain time, like before Benny Goodman, all the bands were pretty much segregated, and then he began to hire Lionel Hampton and Teddy Wilson. But it seemed to me that the music was the one thing that allowed people to go back and forth without all these barriers, you know? Do you see a way that we can use music today to do the same things? Because it seems to me that in the past three or four years particularly, that the barriers are going up again almost. I’d like to see music —

Be integrated more? Yeah, it should be. Well you know they have it in the smaller groups they don’t have the big bands really to mix it more, with more, because we don’t have big bands. But that’s one thing that they never paid much attention to, you know? Of course © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -9-

Benny would do what he wanted to do, and so did Jimmy, Jimmy Dorsey. He had a girl named, black girl named June Richmond and boy she could sing, boy. And he brought her from California all through Texas and everywhere with him. So you’ve got to give him credit for that. This was Jimmy, not Tommy, Jimmy, his brother, you know? And of course Tommy had Charlie Shavers writing in his band, and Sy Oliver was writing all these arrangements. So there was more integration, more. Of course we had more musicians and as I say you had bigger bands and things like that. So I don’t know, let’s see whose got a small group and got it integrated, let’s see — Nancy? I think she’s got an integrated small group. And Carmen McRae — Carmen had an integrated small group. So you know it’s just, the integration is according like with the time now, because you don’t have big bands, you don’t have many integrated musicians because of that.
